description: Game-side values of AdaptOrDeity: the environment (food packets), the colony and the ranges of the player's controls, each with its source. Physiological parameters of the cells are not here: they live upstream in circulatory-autogen-modules modules/cell/generic_adaptive_cell/parameters.json and reach the game inside the assembled kernel (its parameters), so the game reads them from the kernel. Values are canonical SI. status: sourced, placeholder (needs a source), design (a game choice), definitional.

food.packet_trace_minor_share.note: other trace species relative to the main one

food.dry_mass_fraction.note: share of a cell's mass that is not water: E. coli dry weight ~2.8e-13 g of ~9.5e-13 g wet (~30%; 70% water, BioNumbers). A food packet is a dead cell or organic particle of the same make-up (confidence medium: aggregates and mucilage hold more water)

food.dry_carbon_fraction.note: carbon's share of a bacterium's dry mass: ~50% (Neidhardt 1990; BioNumbers). With body.cell_density (1.1 g/mL) and food.dry_mass_fraction (0.3) a packet holds 1100 x 0.3 x 0.5 / 0.012011 = 13,700 mol C/m3, i.e. 2,290 mol glucose equivalents/m3 (2.3 M; 6 C per glucose). Medium confidence: the game counts all of a dead cell's carbon as glucose equivalents, though protein and nucleic acid would need other enzymes

food.carbon_molar_mass.note: molar mass of carbon (IUPAC standard atomic weight 12.011)

food.carbons_per_glucose.note: carbon atoms in a glucose (C6H12O6): a packet's carbon counted in glucose equivalents

food.free_fraction.note: share of a packet's glucose equivalents already small molecules: a bacterium's pool of free metabolites is ~3-4% of its dry mass (E. coli), taken as the same share of its carbon. At the packet density (2.3 M glucose equivalents) that is ~70 mM of free sugar inside the particle, consistent with food.contact_glucose (50 mM at a touching membrane). To check

food.free_leak_rate.note: rate the free small molecules leak out of a packet (a lysed cell): first order, ~10 min time constant; no source yet

food.contact_glucose.note: glucose a cell touching a food packet sees at its membrane (the particle's free sugar, ~70 mM inside it at food.free_fraction of 2.3 M, dissolving into the boundary layer), while the packet lasts. The contact rule takes what the cell takes up from the whole packet, polymer included: the surface hydrolase limits digestion only in the environment field and in a vacuole (engulfing)

food.contact_trace.note: concentration of a packet's main trace species at a touching membrane

food.packet_radius.note: radius of a fresh packet (a dead cell or organic particle): smaller than the 1 um cell (user decision 2026-10-09), within the 0.5-2 um particles of docs/research/food-uptake-and-extracellular-space.md. Its amount is that of a sphere of this radius at the packet density (2.3 M glucose equivalents x 4/3 pi r^3 = 4.9e-15 mol); contact with a cell uses the disc of this radius in the plane (the sphere's equator). As it is eaten it keeps its density, so its radius goes as the cube root of what is left

food.carrier_speed.note: speed of a creature carrying food (prey, or an ally bringing it) over the ground: 1 um/s, slower than a swimming bacterium (~20 um/s) so it can be met

food.lying_density.note: food lying on the ground per area when the field is first filled: about 32 packets in the 30 um view (32 / (30 um)^2), 8x the earlier 4 as packets hold ~8x less (2026-10-12). Later lying food comes with the arrivals

food.used_up_fraction.note: a packet with less than this share of its glucose left is used up and removed

food.entry_angle_spread.note: carried packets enter heading inwards within half this angle either side of the normal

food.field_half_size.note: half the side of the square field around the colony

food.initial_packet_capacity.note: packets the first snapshot frames have room for; frames grow when more are in the field

food.seed.note: random seed of the food field (determinism)

colony.cell_gap.note: gap between neighbouring cells of a colony (centres 2 R_cell + gap apart)

controls.growth_max.note: most ATP a cell may put into growth, in multiples of its resting turnover: growing fermenters run glycolysis 10-40x their maintenance flux; the cell can reach ~40x on food

controls.expression_min.note: lowest expression a player can choose (two octaves below the calibrated cell; user decision 2026-10-08)

controls.expression_max.note: highest expression a player can choose (two octaves above)

environment.current_speed.note: drift of the water over the ground, which carries the creature: a slow near-bed current, 2 um/s (a cell moves with its water; over the sea floor the flow in the viscous sublayer is slow)

motility.mean_run.note: mean length of a run with the motor on (random, exponential; E. coli runs ~1 s between tumbles)

motility.mean_pause.note: mean pause with the motor off between runs (random, exponential); each run sets off in a random direction

motility.seed.note: random seed of the runs and pauses (determinism)

body.cell_density.note: cell density about 1.1 g/mL (BioNumbers): the mass of the body for its momentum, and W/kg for display

motility.thrust_angle_sd.note: standard deviation of each flagellum's thrust direction about straight away from its base: 10 degrees, normal, drawn per run (user decision 2026-10-09); it turns the body, so runs curve

motility.flagellum_spacing.note: where new flagella are placed by default: around the back of the cell, this far apart

skills.glucose_per_point.note: glucose eaten per skill point: calibrated so a level-1 cell left alone for the week earns one 5-point transporter and one kept on food all week two (LevelTests). Re-measured 2026-10-12 with packets at a cell's density (4.9e-15 mol each), field off, food 3e-3 packets/s: left alone it ate 1.69e-13 mol (8 points; ATP gone on day 4, damage 0.32 by day 7); kept on food (0.01 packets/s) 2.98e-13 mol (14 points), the most its carriers take up without growth (4.3e-14 mol a day). The value is unchanged; the outcome is sensitive to the arrival rate and the random sequence (a probe that redrew the arrivals ate 9.45e-14 mol)

skills.points_per_offspring.note: reproduction points: skill points per daughter that leaves the creature at division (no multicellularity), on top of the food points (designer request 2026-10-12: offspring are fitness, so staying single-celled pays for a while). Measured 2026-10-12 (one seed): a level-2 cell kept on food (0.01 packets/s) at growth 3 left 5 daughters in the week (74 food points); at the level's own food (3e-3 packets/s) growth 2-10 runs its ATP out within a day and it leaves none. Set to 1 point per daughter (designer, 2026-10-12)

field.enabled.note: 1 runs the nested environment field: cells take glucose up from it and release lactate and acid into it, food packets dissolve into it; 0 keeps the contact rule (a touching cell sees food.contact_glucose)

field.fine_spacing.note: cell side of the finest grid, around the colony (designer decision 2026-10-12)

field.fine_margin.note: water the finest grid covers beyond the colony on each side: room for the grids to recentre by whole coarse cells (4 um) and for the coarse flux at the fine grid's edge to be away from the cells

field.extent_multiple.note: the outermost grid spans at least this multiple of the colony's diameter (designer decision 2026-10-12); grids have 4x the spacing and extent of the next finer one

field.layer_depth.note: depth of the 2D water layer the field holds: about the distance diffusion mixes in one 0.1 s exchange (sqrt(2 D dt) = 12 um for glucose); the water above it is not represented yet (a 3D correction would add it)

field.diffusivity.glucose.note: glucose in water, 6.73e-10 m2/s at 25 C (about 10% lower at 20 C)

field.diffusivity.lactate.note: lactate anion in water: ~1.0e-9 m2/s, typical of small organic anions; needs a measured value

field.diffusivity.acid.note: the field carries acid as buffered H+ equivalents, moved by the mobile carbonate buffer: bicarbonate's diffusivity at 20 C (1.18e-9 at 25 C). Free H+ (9.3e-9) is ~1e-4 of the acid at pH 7.3, so its own diffusion is negligible

field.diffusivity.oxygen.note: O2 in water at ~20-25 C (2.0e-9 at 20 C, 2.4e-9 at 25 C in Han & Bartels; 2.1e-9 used)

field.diffusivity.aspartate.note: amino acids of aspartate's size diffuse at ~0.8-0.9e-9 m2/s at 25 C (glycine 1.06e-9, alanine 0.91e-9); aspartate's own value to check

field.diffusivity.serine.note: near alanine's 0.91e-9 m2/s at 25 C; serine's own value to check

field.diffusivity.ribose.note: a pentose, a little faster than glucose (6.73e-10 at 25 C); to check

field.diffusivity.dimethylsulfide.note: dimethyl sulfide in water at ~20 C; value to check against the paper

environment.oxygen.note: O2 in the surface ocean at ~0.1% of present atmospheric O2 (mid-Proterozoic estimate); 0.25 mol/m3 today at 20 C. Nothing takes it up yet

environment.carbonate_total.note: dissolved inorganic carbon of the 2 Ga ocean: ~10 PAL CO2 (paleosols ~2.2 Ga) gives ~0.15 mM CO2 and ~3 mM HCO3- at pH 7.3. Sets the buffer that turns acid into pH

environment.carbonate_pk1.note: first carbonic acid dissociation constant (pK1*) in seawater at ~20 C, S 35; to check

field.input_tolerance.note: a cell's membrane concentrations from the field reach its module only when they moved by more than this share since they last did: every changed input restarts the cell's integrator, and the field moves a little every step (colony-bench 512 cells, 20 s, environment field: 4.0 s with every change passed, 3.0 s at 1e-3, 1.5 s at 1e-2; 0.6 s on the contact rule). The exchange stays exact (it uses the cell's own fluxes)

field.reference_substeps.note: field steps per macro step in the reference environment (FieldAccuracy.Reference): lambda = D dt / dx^2 about 1.6 for the acid at 1 um and 0.1/64 s; tests check the reference is converged in it

field.reference_cell_tolerance.note: cells relative tolerance in the reference environment

prey.radius.note: radius of a prey cell: half the creature's 1 um cell, so a cell can engulf it (marine bacteria are often 0.2-1 um across). Its content is a sphere of this radius at the packet density (1.2e-15 mol glucose equivalents), with the packet's free share

prey.run_speed.note: swimming speed of prey over the ground during a run: 3 um/s, slower than swimming bacteria (20-30 um/s) so the creature can meet them

prey.mean_run.note: mean run before a tumble (exponential); each tumble sets a new heading at random. E. coli runs ~1 s

prey.initial_capacity.note: prey the first snapshot frames have room for; frames grow when more are in view

organisms.max.note: most free-living organisms (released daughters and their offspring) simulated at once; a new daughter beyond it replaces a dead one, else the one farthest from the creature (counted as gone). Measured cost: see docs/plans/free-daughters.md

organisms.range_view_widths.note: a free organism farther than this many view widths (2 x food.field_half_size) from the creature, along either ground axis, is no longer simulated (gone out of range); beyond the view it sees only the open water, with no food packets

organisms.dead_kept.note: how long a dead free organism stays in the water (drifting, drawn grey) before it is removed; it does not become food yet

organisms.initial_capacity.note: free organisms the first snapshot frames have room for; frames grow when there are more

trace_species.name: Aspartate
trace_species.note: an E. coli Tar attractant (adapting_plan.md: smell at level 3)

trace_species.name: Ribose
trace_species.note: sensed through Trg and the ribose-binding protein

trace_species.name: Dimethyl sulfide
trace_species.note: a marine infochemical of algal origin
